name: Tabeel
title: The Proposed Puppet King
summary: Tabeel is an obscure figure mentioned in Isaiah 7:6 as the son of a man with the same or similar name. During the Syro-Ephraimite War, King Rezin of Aram and King Pekah of Israel planned to depose King Ahaz of Judah and install Tabeel's son as a puppet king in Jerusalem. The plan failed when God, through the prophet Isaiah, assured Ahaz that this conspiracy would not succeed.

keyEvents.title: The Syro-Ephraimite Conspiracy
keyEvents.description: King Rezin of Aram and King Pekah of Israel planned to invade Judah, depose King Ahaz, and replace him with Tabeel's son as a compliant puppet king.

keyEvents.title: God's Assurance through Isaiah
keyEvents.description: The prophet Isaiah delivered God's message to King Ahaz that the conspiracy against Judah would not succeed and that the plan to install Tabeel's son would fail.

keyEvents.title: The Immanuel Sign
keyEvents.description: In connection with the threat from the coalition, God gave the sign of Immanuel through Isaiah as a promise of His presence and protection of David's dynasty against this conspiracy.

keyEvents.title: The Coalition's Attack on Judah
keyEvents.description: The historical context for Tabeel's role is also found in the Books of Kings, where the attack by Aram and Israel against Judah during King Ahaz's reign is described.
